test_title: PYST 46: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 24 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a window provided by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for banks to borrow overnight funds at a higher interest rate than the repo rate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Marginal Standing Facility**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)** is a liquidity adjustment facility provided by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to banks, enabling them to borrow overnight funds.
 
• It was introduced in **May 2011** by the RBI as a part of its monetary policy framework to manage short-term liquidity mismatches.
 
• The MSF rate is set at **100 basis points (1%) higher** than the repo rate, making it a costlier option for banks compared to the repo rate.
 
• Banks can access MSF by pledging their **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) securities** beyond the mandatory requirement up to a certain limit.
 
• MSF is primarily used by banks during periods of acute liquidity stress, acting as a safety valve for the banking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Repo Rate**

 
 
• It is the rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks for short-term needs, typically to control inflation and liquidity.
 
• The repo rate is a critical tool in the RBI's monetary policy to influence borrowing and lending in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**
 
 
• It is the minimum percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be maintained in the form of liquid assets like cash, gold, or approved securities.
 
• SLR is a tool used by the RBI to regulate bank credit expansion and ensure financial stability.
 
 
 
• **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)**
 
 
• LAF is a mechanism through which the RBI manages liquidity and provides short-term funds to banks via repo and reverse repo operations.
 
• It helps in maintaining monetary stability and ensuring that liquidity conditions align with the monetary policy stance.
 
 
 
• **Standing Deposit Facility (SDF)**
 
 
• It is a tool introduced by the RBI in April 2022 to absorb excess liquidity from the banking system without the need for collateral.
 
• The SDF rate is set below the repo rate, functioning as the floor of the liquidity adjustment corridor.
